brief: US high-yield credit is not breaking broadly: investment grade, broad high yield and single-B spreads remain contained. The fracture is concentrated at the bottom of the quality ladder. The single-B to CCC jump is about 8 percentage points, and the CCC minus single-B spread has widened to 799bp, near the top of its three-year range and above the roughly 575bp median (BofA). Small-cap equities are starting to reflect this: Bloomberg Caa spreads reached 9.2%, their widest since 2023, and the Russell 2000 has lost more than 8% relative to the S&P 500 since late June (BTIG). BTIG finds 11 similar occasions since 1996, where the pattern was not an immediate S&P 500 collapse but further Russell weakness over the following 40-60 trading days. What has not moved is small-cap options pricing: the six-month IWM-versus-SPX implied-volatility spread has fallen near the bottom of its two-year range (GS), so Russell volatility stays cheap relative to large caps despite the financing risk. The suggested expression is an IWM Nov 280/265 put spread.
